initial_prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a simple polished concept illustration for a DIY surveying rig, using the supplied image only as a reference for relative pole/bracket/Avia/receiver arrangement. Show a complete adult surveyor from head to shoes holding one slim vertical black carbon-fibre Emlid survey pole, about 2 m long, tip on the ground. On top: simplified light grey Emlid Reach RS4 Pro GNSS receiver, about 128.6 mm diameter and 99.3 mm tall. About 210 mm below its base: the compact dark rectangular Livox Avia sensor pointing outwards and 20 degrees downwards, on the orange sensor bracket and blue split clamp visible in the reference. Add a small dark rectangular weatherproof Raspberry Pi enclosure strapped to the pole about 250 mm below the Avia, on the opposite side, with a simple short cable routed neatly along the pole. Person holds pole lower down so equipment remains fully visible. Neutral clean off-white background, understated editorial 3D/isometric illustration, modest detail, accurate believable scale, face generic. Place small clean Norwegian callout labels with thin leader lines: 'Emlid Reach RS4 Pro', 'Livox Avia - 20° ned', 'Ø35 mm landmålerstang', 'RPi-boks'. Small footer exactly 'Prinsippskisse - ikke målfast'. Full person, pole, receiver, Avia, clamp and Pi box all inside the image. Do not reproduce logos, manufacturer CAD detailing, website art, or product photographs. No tripod, no drone, no extra receivers. Reference picture is simplified independent CAD geometry, not a target to edit. The final image should be a new scene with a person, not just the CAD screenshot.
